question: Do the Action Plan and the MPRs address all potential pollution contributors within the PRS catchment?
intro: For every focus region in the catchment - towns (ULBs), industrial areas and gram panchayats - this section compares what the KSPCB Action Plan committed to with what the monthly progress reports (MPRs) actually report. Where a row says 'not reported', that means absent from the documents, not necessarily absent on the ground.

primary.label: NMCG Monthly Progress Report (Karnataka, Arkavathi stretch)

actionPlan.label: KSPCB Action Plan for Rejuvenation of River Arkavathi (January 2019, mirrored)

baseline.banner: MPR editions from October 2025 onward no longer report PRS-wise status. Accountability tracking below therefore anchors on the last PRS-wise reporting.
otherSources: District Environment Plans (Ramanagara 2021, Bengaluru Urban 2022) - one-time snapshots
CAG Report No. 8 of 2017 (KIADB CETP audit)

solid-waste.label: NGT OA 606/2018 - SWM Rules compliance (Justice Subhash B Adi committee)
SWM Rules 2016 (KSPCB guidelines hub); SWM Rules 2026 in force from 1 Apr 2026

biomedical.label: NGT OA 710/2017 (Shailesh Singh vs Sheela Hospital & Others) - BMW Rules 2016

fecal-sludge.label: SC (2017) 5 SCC 326 - mandatory sewage treatment infrastructure; NGT OA 673/2018 monitoring

public-stps.label: SC (2017) 5 SCC 326 - mandatory treatment infrastructure; NGT OA 673/2018 monthly reporting

private-stps.label: GoK notification FEE 316 EPC 2015 as amended 12.03.2024 - who must install STPs and reuse treated water (mirrored)
KSPCB OCEMS mandate for private STPs above 500 KLD (RTI response, Jul 2026; earlier media reports said 100 KLD)

effluent.label: Water Act consent regime; CAG Report No. 8 of 2017 on missing CETPs; NGT OA 1038/2018 (Peenya CEPI)

hazardous.label: H&OW (M&TM) Rules 2016; KSPCB hazardous waste management (authorised recyclers list)

regions.name: Ramanagara (CMC)
regions.inBasinNote: Stretch ULB - on the Arkavathi mainstem; population 95,167 (2011). One of only two ULBs the MPRs itemise.

categories.label: Solid Waste

actionPlan.summary: Finalise the MSW processing site and manage the two towns' ~75 TPD properly; caution boards and penalties for river-bank dumping (actions 3 and 5). In 2019 the plan records Ramanagara had not identified a disposal site.

mpr.summary: 40 TPD generated, 35 collected, only 15 processed; ~20 TPD to landfill and a 20-24 TPD management gap. SWM DPR approved under Swachh Bharat Mission, 'action being taken as per DPR'.

gaps: Bulk waste generators, their compliance and waste processing destinations are not mentioned in any MPR (SWM Rules 2016 Rule 4 requires bulk generators to process in-situ).
The processed fraction (15 of 40 TPD) has not moved across MPR editions - status effectively unchanged since the plan.

categories.label: Biomedical Waste

actionPlan.summary: The January 2019 Action Plan does not mention biomedical waste at all.
actionPlan.cite: Action Plan Jan 2019 (full text, zero mentions)

mpr.summary: 0.208 TPD generated across 460 hospitals and health-care facilities; common treatment facility (CBMWTF) status: 'complying'.

gaps: A one-word 'complying' with no facility name, capacity or inspection trail - the CAG has separately criticised KSPCB's biomedical-waste tracking.

media.label: TOI: Toxic negligence - KSPCB fails to track biomedical waste, says CAG

categories.label: Fecal Sludge

actionPlan.summary: Faecal sludge, septage and FSTPs do not appear in the January 2019 Action Plan.
actionPlan.cite: Action Plan Jan 2019 (full text, zero mentions)

mpr.summary: 4.0 MLD of Ramanagara's sewage is handled through septic tanks and soak pits (the unsewered share) - but no faecal-sludge treatment plant is reported operational anywhere in the basin; Harohalli's 6 KLD planted drying bed is work-in-progress.

gaps: Where the collected septage from 4.0 MLD-worth of septic tanks actually goes is not reported in any MPR.

categories.label: Public STPs

actionPlan.summary: 100% UGD with full collection network and 100% treatment; silk-unit effluent routed to the CMC STP; O&M budget of Rs 0.486 crore/year for the existing 7.5 MLD STP (actions 1-2, cost table).

mpr.summary: One 7.5 MLD STP, 6.0 MLD utilised, operational but NON-COMPLYING; 11 drains still to be connected; 'No Work Progress' against a completion timeline of 31.12.2021; Rs 220.17 crore DPR for missing links and STP upgradation submitted to GoK by KUWS&DB.

gaps: The completion timeline lapsed in December 2021; successive MPRs repeat the same 'DPR submitted' status - the reported gap of 4.0 MLD has held for four+ years.
STP non-compliance is reported without parameter-level detail or enforcement action.

categories.label: Private STPs

actionPlan.summary: Private/apartment STPs are not mentioned in the Action Plan.

mpr.summary: No MPR edition reports private STP counts, capacities, compliance or treated-water reuse for Ramanagara.

gaps: The GoK STP mandate (2016/2024) applies to qualifying apartments and commercial buildings here too - nothing in the public record shows whether any exist or comply.

regions.name: Kanakapura (CMC)
regions.inBasinNote: Stretch ULB - downstream end of the polluted stretch; population 54,014 (2011). The second of the two ULBs the MPRs itemise.

categories.label: Solid Waste

actionPlan.summary: Same commitment as Ramanagara: finalise the MSW processing site (unidentified in 2019) and stop river-bank dumping.

mpr.summary: 24 TPD generated, 10 processed; processing facility reported 'under construction'.

gaps: Bulk generators and waste destinations not mentioned; 'under construction' status persists across editions.

categories.label: Biomedical Waste

actionPlan.summary: Not mentioned in the Action Plan.

gaps: Same one-word compliance reporting as Ramanagara - no facility detail.

actionPlan.summary: Not mentioned in the Action Plan.

mpr.summary: 0.6 MLD handled via septic tanks and soak pits; no FSTP reported for the town.

categories.label: Public STPs

actionPlan.summary: 100% UGD and treatment; O&M budget Rs 0.384 crore/year for the 6.29 MLD STP.

mpr.summary: One 6.29 MLD STP, 3.8 MLD utilised, operational but NON-COMPLYING; 5 drains still to be connected to the STP.

gaps: Non-compliance persists across editions with no enforcement trail.

mpr.summary: No private-STP reporting for Kanakapura in any edition.

regions.name: Bengaluru (BBMP) - V-Valley catchment
regions.inBasinNote: Catchment-scoped entry: the Vrishabhavathi valley inside BBMP is the stretch's largest upstream load. Scope here is limited to what the MPRs report for the V-Valley; this is not a whole-city audit.

categories.label: Public STPs (BWSSB, V-Valley)

actionPlan.summary: New V-Valley STPs to treat 100% of sewage: Nayandanahalli 150 MLD (Rs 470 crore) and Doddabele 40 MLD (Rs 73 crore), both 'work under progress' in 2019; O&M budget Rs 3.5 crore/year for existing BWSSB STPs (action 4, cost table).

mpr.summary: MPRs track the V-Valley STP fleet (500 + 180 + 75 + 60 + 10 + 1 MLD units per the plan's Table-1) and treated-water reuse volumes (~1.08 MLD sewage + ~3.32 MLD trade effluent recycled).

gaps: Untreated overflow into the Vrishabhavathi persists; per-STP compliance for the V-Valley fleet is not itemised PRS-wise.

categories.label: Industrial effluent (V-Valley)

actionPlan.summary: Inventorisation of catchment industries (3 months), action against non-consented units (6 months), channelisation of effluent to CETPs (18 months), OCEMS for red-category units (marked 'complied' already in 2019).

mpr.summary: 191 industries reported in the V-Valley catchment (Red-31, Orange-60, Green-97, White-3), effluent 'treated and recycled' - while the KSPCB F-register lists ~7,000 consented industries in Peenya + Dasarahalli alone. See the Industrial effluent stressor for the full denominator story.

gaps: The MPR's 191-industry universe vs the F-register's ~7,000 is the central unexplained discrepancy.

regions.name: Magadi (TMC)
regions.inBasinNote: In-basin ULB on the upper Arkavathi (TG Halli catchment).
regions.silentNote: Not itemised in any MPR edition we hold: no sewage, solid waste, biomedical, faecal sludge or STP reporting at ULB level. The only public snapshot is the one-time District Environment Plan (2021/2022).

regions.name: Nelamangala (TMC)
regions.inBasinNote: In-basin ULB on the Kumudavathi arm (TG Halli catchment); ~1,950 consented industries in its KSPCB regional-office register (2019).
regions.silentNote: Not itemised in any MPR edition we hold - the deck's exemplar ULB for exactly this gap. District Environment Plan (2022) is the only public snapshot.

regions.name: Doddaballapura (CMC)
regions.inBasinNote: In-basin ULB at the Arkavathi headwaters; ~1,450 consented industries in its regional-office register (2019), incl. the Doddaballapura industrial area.
regions.silentNote: Not itemised in any MPR edition we hold.

regions.name: Bidadi (TP)
regions.inBasinNote: In-basin town on the lower Vrishabhavathi, adjoining the Bidadi industrial area.
regions.silentNote: Not itemised in any MPR edition we hold; appears only in the DEP snapshot and in industrial-area actions (CETP).

regions.name: Harohalli (TP)
regions.inBasinNote: In-basin town adjoining the Harohalli industrial area; the basin's only reported FSTP (6 KLD, work-in-progress) is here.
regions.silentNote: Not itemised as a ULB in any MPR edition we hold - only its industrial area and the FSTP appear.

regions.name: Peenya Industrial Area
regions.inBasinNote: The basin's industrial core (~5,070 consented industries, 2019 F-register); CPCB Critically Polluted Area (CEPI 78.12); drains to the Vrishabhavathi.

categories.label: Industrial effluent / CETP

actionPlan.summary: Commissioning of a 200 KLD CETP at Peenya, Rs 10 crore, 'tender under process' (2019); channelisation of effluents to CETPs within 18 months.
actionPlan.cite: Action Plan Jan 2019, cost table item 5, action I(j)-(k)

mpr.summary: The Peenya CETP appears in the Action Plan but is not mentioned in later MPR editions - no commissioning, tender-progress or abandonment status has been reported since.

gaps: A committed Rs 10 crore CETP has simply vanished from the reporting trail - the deck's exemplar accountability gap.

categories.label: Hazardous waste

actionPlan.summary: Hazardous waste management is not a plan action beyond general compliance.

mpr.summary: Stretch-level totals only (~4,033 MTPA from 97 industries); no TSDF details ('NA') and nothing Peenya-specific.

gaps: Groundwater contamination by heavy metals in Peenya is acknowledged in the plan itself (electroplating clusters, studies since 2012) but has no tracked action.

regions.name: Bidadi Industrial Area
regions.inBasinNote: KIADB area on the lower Vrishabhavathi; industries directed in 2019 to contribute to river rejuvenation.

categories.label: Industrial effluent / CETP

actionPlan.summary: 50 KLD CETP, Rs 2.5 crore, site identification + commissioning by KIADB within 24 months.
actionPlan.cite: Action Plan Jan 2019, cost table item 5, action I(k)

mpr.summary: No commissioning or progress status for the Bidadi CETP in later MPR editions.

gaps: CAG (2017) found KIADB areas without CETPs and ~2,571 ML/yr untreated discharge - the plan's response has no reported follow-through.

regions.name: Harohalli Industrial Area
regions.inBasinNote: KIADB area south of Bidadi; F-register/OCEMS show pharma units (Neoanthem) enrolled for effluent monitoring.

actionPlan.summary: 50 KLD CETP, Rs 2.5 crore, by KIADB within 24 months.
actionPlan.cite: Action Plan Jan 2019, cost table item 5

mpr.summary: No CETP status reported in later editions.

categories.label: Fecal sludge / soak pits

actionPlan.summary: Industrial-area sewage/septage is not a plan item.

mpr.summary: Industries in the stretch report disposing sewage (~0.02 MLD at the two Acchalu units) to individual septic tanks and soak pits; the 6 KLD Harohalli FSTP (planted drying bed, Rs 350 lakh) remains work-in-progress.

gaps: Soak-pit disposal by industries is reported as an endpoint with no septage trail.

regions.name: Kumbalagodu Industrial Area
regions.inBasinNote: KIADB area on the Vrishabhavathi (Kengeri hobli); hosts two private CETPs (Pai & Pai Chemicals) - the only two CETPs existing in the stretch per the plan; heavy-metal and PPCP studies cluster here.

categories.label: Industrial effluent / CETP

actionPlan.summary: The plan records the two existing private CETPs at Kumbalagodu as the stretch's only treatment; no new commitment for the area itself.

mpr.summary: Covered only inside V-Valley catchment aggregates; no Kumbalagodu-specific reporting. Independent studies (2009 heavy metals; 2018-19 PPCPs incl. ibuprofen 1,834 ng/L; Paani x ICCW 2024 Site F nearby at BOD ~107 mg/L) document the load.

gaps: The stretch's only CETPs have no public compliance reporting.

regions.name: Dabaspet Industrial Area
regions.inBasinNote: KIADB area in the Kumudavathi/TG Halli catchment (Nelamangala side); OCEMS-enrolled units include Bio-gen Extracts.
regions.silentNote: Not mentioned in the Action Plan or itemised in any MPR edition we hold - visible only through the F-register denominator and OCEMS enrolment.

regions.name: Doddaballapura Industrial Area
regions.inBasinNote: Textile-heavy KIADB area at the Arkavathi headwaters; Ramky Enviro's hazardous-waste incinerator (OCEMS-enrolled) sits here.
regions.silentNote: Not mentioned in the Action Plan or itemised in any MPR edition we hold.

regions.name: Gram Panchayats (258 in basin)
regions.inBasinNote: The basin's rural local bodies - including every village along the polluted stretch outside the two CMCs.
regions.silentNote: No MPR edition and no Action Plan item reports anything at gram-panchayat level: no sewage, solid waste, faecal sludge or water-quality responsibility is itemised for any of the 258 GPs. Rural reaches of the stretch are effectively unreported in the official accountability trail.
